summary: Smooths line-strip attributes, usually P, by blending neighboring values along the strip. It can smooth by edge distance or point steps, use Gaussian or box weighting, optionally pre-divide curves, and map smoothing parameters per point.

key_concepts: Line Smooth filters attributes along each line strip, usually P, and therefore can change the visible curve shape.
Edge-distance filtering gives spatially consistent smoothing on uneven samples, while point-step filtering uses neighboring vertex counts.
Pre-divide, endpoint locking, optional resampling, and parameter maps let smoothing preserve anchors while varying strength along the strip.
common_gotchas: Smoothing by point steps can include far-away points on unevenly sampled curves; use edge distance for spatially consistent smoothing.
End Points Fixed is important for curves that must stay attached to anchors or input endpoints.
Pre-divide increases density before smoothing, so maxverts must be sized for the pre-divided result.
